verification_method: The script's stdout is fully buffered (redirected to a file, not a TTY) and print() was not called with flush=True or python3 -u, so periodic progress lines have not yet been written to the log file despite 4258s of continuous execution -- this is a real limitation of the launch command (a known, disclosed gap), not evidence of a stall by itself. Process liveness and forward progress were instead verified directly via two non-invasive `sample <pid> 1` stack-trace snapshots (macOS sample(1), 1ms sampling interval, no signal sent to the process, does not pause or affect it) taken 8 seconds apart. Both snapshots show CPU-bound execution deep inside real pandas/pyarrow code paths consistent with the replay's own DataFrame slicing and attribute resolution (_PyObject_GenericGetAttrWithDict, CachedProperty, pyarrow_wrap_data_type, dict_getitem, etc.) -- not a repeating idle loop, not a blocked syscall, not the same frame twice. The two stack traces differ (58 of 58 compared lines changed), and CPU time (4231s) tracks wall-clock elapsed time (4258s) at ~99% utilization, consistent with continuous single-threaded computation rather than an I/O wait or hang.
no_second_writer_method: ps aux | grep -i python shows exactly one process running _phase5_causal_replay.py (PID 13104); the only other Python processes on the host are an unrelated long-running app.py dev server (PID 74525, started Monday, unrelated to this experiment) and an unrelated VS Code language-server helper.
note_for_future_runs: Future long-running replay scripts in this experiment should be launched with `python3 -u` (or explicit flush=True on progress prints) so log progress is visible without needing indirect stack-sampling verification. This is a monitoring/observability gap in how the process was launched, not a defect in the replay logic itself, and does not by itself indicate any problem with the experiment's correctness.
estimate_revision: Original estimate assumed ~64-138ms per decision-point evaluation based on a 200-point smoke test (27.7s / 200 = 138ms/point), projecting ~85 minutes for 37,152 points. Actual elapsed time (71 minutes) with no observed completion suggests either a materially slower true per-call rate at full scale (plausible given pandas/pyarrow attribute-resolution overhead visible in the stack samples) or simply that the smoke-test rate held and full completion is imminent. Will be resolved definitively once the process exits and produces its output files; continuing to monitor rather than estimating further.
